# Held out results

*Generated by `python -m antenatal holdout-report` on 2026-10-24T09:34:32+00:00 from the tables the single held out evaluation wrote, the access log, the integrity audits and git. Nothing was fitted and the held out records were not read to produce this page. The protocol fixed before the run is `docs/holdout_protocol.md`.*

The held out records are 782 pregnancies with 41 recorded low birth weight births. They were set aside before any model was fitted and evaluated once, at 2026-10-24T09:22:37+00:00, on models locked beforehand. Nothing about the models changes because of these results.

## 1. Proof that the model did not learn from the held out records

The supervisor asked that the held out records never be found in the training pipeline, so that the model could not be biased by them. Five separate kinds of evidence show this.

**1. The order of events, from git.** The held out records were sealed before the served model was fitted, every locked model was fixed before the held out outcomes were first read, and no locked model changed afterwards.

| Event | File | Commit and time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Held out records sealed (their checksum) | `partitions/holdout.sha256` | 200e93b 2026-10-21 17:13:52 +0200 |
| Served model (set C, 1.0.0) last changed | `webapp/model/lbw_model.joblib` | 51b514f 2026-10-21 17:43:15 +0200 |
| Set B comparator frozen | `webapp/model/secondary_set_b/lbw_model.joblib` | 026bcd5 2026-10-21 18:27:25 +0200 |
| Label threshold fixed | `webapp/model/classification.json` | 527dd46 2026-10-23 17:02:17 +0200 |
| Set A comparator frozen | `webapp/model/comparator_set_a/lbw_model.joblib` | c551a26 2026-10-24 03:39:31 +0200 |
| Integrity audit before the run committed | `docs/evidence/holdout_run/audit_before.txt` | 55ef108 2026-10-24 11:22:04 +0200 |
| Held out outcomes read for the first time | `partitions/holdout_access.log` | 2026-10-24T09:22:11+00:00 |

**2. The integrity audit, before and after.** `python -m antenatal audit-holdout` checks, without reading any held out outcome, that no held out record is in the development data, that no registration group is split between the two, that the training guard refuses every held out record, that no saved prediction file contains a held out record, that the served model reproduces the development out of fold predictions, and that no held out record has a predictor vector identical to a development record. Before the run 11 of 11 checks passed (`docs/evidence/holdout_run/audit_before.txt`, committed before the run); after the run 11 of 11 passed (`docs/evidence/holdout_integrity.md`).

**3. The guard in code.** Every model fit carries a `TrainingGuard` that raises an error if any held out record is present, and every step that learns from data (imputation, scaling, the availability screen, tuning) runs inside the training fold.

**4. Rebuilding the model from development records alone.** `tests/integration/test_artefact_reproducibility.py` refits the served pipeline on the 3,126 development records only and checks that its feature names, coefficients, intercept and reference probabilities equal those of the committed model to within 1e-9. A model that had seen any held out record could not be rebuilt exactly without it.

**5. One read, logged.** `partitions/holdout_access.log` holds 3 lines: the opening of the partition, 1 evaluation with the operator, purpose, commit and every checksum, and 1 refused attempt to evaluate again.

**What the results themselves show.** A model that had learned from the held out records would score clearly better on them than on unseen development records. The table compares the served model on both.

| Calibration intercept | -0.0018 (-0.1675 to 0.1504) | -0.0127 (-0.3694 to 0.2656) | yes |

## 2. Reading the results

* The primary comparison, C over B (first visit added) on Average precision, is +0.0012 and its interval contains zero. The smallest difference these records could detect is 0.0274.
* The secondary comparison, B over A (second visit added) on ROC AUC, is +0.0405 and its interval excludes zero. The smallest difference these records could detect is 0.0573.
* For the served model, 7 of 9 held out estimates fall inside the interval of the same measure on development records.
* The held out ROC AUC (0.5725) is worse than on development records (0.6281).
* The held out calibration slope (0.4475) is worse than on development records (0.9788).
* The held out ROC AUC interval includes 0.5, the value of ranking at random, so on these records the served model's discrimination cannot be told apart from chance.
* Every held out estimate outside its development interval is worse, not better, which is the opposite of what a model that had learned from these records would show.

With 41 events every interval is wide. An interval that contains zero does not show that two models are equal; it shows that these records cannot tell them apart.
